title: How He Got A Software Engineering Job With No Experience
description:
How He Got A Software Engineering Job With No Experience


He sent nearly 700 applications in a year and got 2 interviews. If you are trying to break into software engineering with no commercial experience, and every developer job wants years you do not have, the problem is not your coding, it is your approach. This is the exact story of how one self-taught developer got a software engineering job with no experience, at a company asking for 3 years he did not have, and the 3 moves that turned a year of rejection into a £40,000 offer in about 8 weeks.

This is for anyone trying to land their first software engineering or developer job and stuck in the applying-and-hearing-nothing loop.


What you'll learn in this video:
- Why a software engineering job description is a wish list, not a wall, and how to get hired without the years it asks for
- The 1 move that beats 100 online applications: going straight to the engineer or founder who owns the role
- How to flip a lack of experience into a reason to hire you instead of an apology
- What actually gets scored in a coding take-home and a technical interview (it is not writing perfect code)
- How one self-taught developer went from 2 interviews in a year to final rounds at 4 companies at once


VIDEO CHAPTERS:
0:00 700 applications, 2 interviews, then a £40k software engineering offer
0:17 The one thing he changed
0:47 A job description is a wish list, not a wall
1:23 Move 1: go to the person who owns the role
2:36 Move 2: turn the experience gap into their win
3:55 Move 3: win the room as a peer
5:02 The result: final rounds at 4 companies at once
5:35 What to do today


Not getting interviews and not sure what is actually stopping you? Start here:

FREE DIAGNOSIS:
Take the free 2-minute diagnosis. Get your personalised employability score plus a roadmap of exactly what to fix first in your job search.
https://the.offeraccelerator.uk/new-candidate-diagnosis?source=youtube&utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=description&utm_campaign=software-engineering-job-no-experience


CONNECT WITH ME
LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/olivercordingley
Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/olivercordingley


WATCH NEXT:
How to Get Hired With Zero Experience


ABOUT ME:
I dropped out of university at 19 to build recruitment software and ATS systems used by hiring teams. For years I spoke to hundreds of hiring managers and recruiters every day, learning exactly how candidates get filtered, shortlisted, and hired from the inside. I started coaching friends through their job search using what I'd seen, then raised investment, built a software company, and hired my own team. I've seen hiring from every angle.

Today I help job seekers land offers faster using a proven 3-step system. I've coached hundreds of candidates into roles at firms like JP Morgan, Goldman Sachs, Deloitte, EY, and PwC and many more.

transcript: Ebrahim sent just under 700 applications in a year and he got two interviews, both at the same company. And then what he did is he changed one thing and he landed a 40,000 pound offer as a junior software engineer at Muz, a company that was openly asking for 3 years of experience that he never actually had. And the one thing that he changed comes down to this. He stopped trying to look qualified on paper and he started giving them a reason to bet on him directly. And that is the whole job search game now. He's not a better coder than the thousands of people who got rejected that year. He didn't go and get more experience. He just changed how he went after the job and it turned around in about 8 weeks. So if you're trying to break into software engineering and every role wants experience that you don't have yet, this is exactly how he got in anyway. And I'm going to walk you through those three moves he made using, you know, his actual story. So here's the thing that almost nobody gets about going for a software engineering job that you're under qualified for. That job description isn't a wall, it's a wish list. So when a company writes, you know, "3 years of experience", what they really mean is that I need someone who won't fall apart when the work sort of gets hard and I don't want to take a risk on the wrong person. Now experience is just the easiest shortcut for them to feel safe. So your job was never to go magically invent some experience and get some, is to make them feel safe hiring you without actually having the experience. And that's a completely different game to firing off hundreds of applications, which is actually good news for you because it means that the thing that gets you in isn't the thing that you're missing. So the first move that Ebrahim made is that he stopped feeding the pipeline and he went straight to the person who actually owns the job. So for a whole year, he did what everyone else does. He uses CV templates, he started applying to job boards, he asked his friends and family for referrals and it just slowly dried up. Because when you drop your CV into an online form, the first thing that happens is you get screened out on that 3 years line long before an engineer who actually cares even sees you. So the person who actually owns the role can do something a form can't, they can make an exception. So Ebrahim got in front of a person who owned that hiring decision, the company's technical founder, at an in-person meetup and he put his work straight in front of him instead of just a pile with 300 candidates there. And that one conversation got him a call booked with no CV sitting in a queue. So, the way you use this is simple. I want you to take 10 to 15 companies who you actually want to work at. Instead of hunting for the recruiter, find the person who would actually manage you. Maybe the engineer or the technical founder or the CTO. Then go to where they already are. A meetup, a post they wrote, a comment section, a direct email. And when you reach out, lead with their work and a genuine question, not sort of like please refer I mean. So, one real with the person who owns the role beats hundreds of applications being sent into the void. Now, the second move is where most people lose it. And it's the reframe that actually got Ibrahim hired. So, when you're under qualified, the natural instinct is just to apologize for it. You know, you get in the room and you go and go, "Look, I know I don't have 3 years of experience, but and then you make a lot of excuses." And the second that you say that, you've just agreed with their objection for them. Now, Ibrahim, he did the opposite. He didn't hide the gap. He actually reframed it. On that call, he showed them actual systems that and he talked through the decisions he made and why he made them. And he told them exactly what he owned in the first 90 days of him starting the job. Now, he answered the real question the hiring manager was asking, which was Now, in that presentation, he answered the real question the hiring manager was asking, which was never actually, you know, do you have 3 years of experience? It was, "Can this person do the work and will I be glad that I hired them?" And that works because experience is really just a stand-in for trust. If you can show the thinking and the ownership directly, you hand them that trust without the years on your CV. So, here's how you apply it. For every real thing that you've built on or worked on, you need to be able to say in your own words out loud what the problem was, what you decided, and what happened. So, if you can't defend a line on your CV in a normal conversation, it isn't doing anything for you. And have a specific answer ready for what you do in the first 90 days of starting the job because being specific beats that humble presentation every time. And then the third move is how he actually won the room because he still had to get through a real hiring process. Now, there was an interview, then a take-home coding task, and then a call with the founders. And this is where under-qualified people usually fall apart because they walk in trying to look perfect and then come across as rehearsed and nervous instead. So, take that coding task, and most people pour everything into making the code flawless. What actually mattered was the short write-up next to it, where he explained, you know, how he thought about the problem, the assumptions that he made, why he chose what he chose, and what he would do with more than that. The assumptions that he made, why he chose the decisions that he chose, and what he would do if he had more time. Now, senior engineers skim that in a couple of minutes, and they're judging how you think, not whether it was perfect. And in the interviews, he didn't go quiet and hand over a finished answer. He talked through this thinking out loud so that they could actually watch how he works out a problem. And he walked in like a peer, not someone just begging for a shot or a chance. And he also came in with real questions for them, like, "What's the biggest technical problem that the team is trying to solve this year?" Because people don't really remember your exact answers. They remember whether it felt good to talk to you, and whether they could actually picture you in their team. So, he ran that same play across a few companies at once, and a year after getting two interviews, he was in the final rounds at Google, and at Immersive Labs, Deloitte, and Moz all at the same time. Now, Moz are the ones who gave him the offer as a junior back-end engineer on 40K base, and he even pushed that number up himself when it landed. And the reason why I'm sharing all of this is that not one of those three moves needed more experience. They just needed a completely different approach to the thing you're already doing every single day. So, if you're stuck in that mass application place right now, the most useful thing you can do is find out what's actually stopping you because it's usually not what you think it is. Now, I built a free 2-minute diagnosis that scores where you're at and tells you the first thing that you need to fix. Now, it's completely free, and the link is in the description if you want to check it out. But whatever you do, stop feeding the application pipeline. Go straight to the person who owns the role, show them how you actually think, and give them a reason to bet on you before anyone else gets the chance to ask about your experience.

title: The secret to getting referrals from people you don't know
description:
Stop Asking To Pick Their Brain | How To Network To Get A Job


Most job seekers send the same networking message, can I pick your brain, and then wonder why nobody ever replies. The truth is 72% of jobs are filled through referrals and internal networks, and only 28% come from job boards. This video gives you a 6-step networking system to network into a job: who to message, what to actually say so people reply, and the Impact Loop that turns one reply into a referral and an interview.

If you have been applying online and hearing nothing back, networking is the side door into the 72% of roles you cannot see. This is the full system I teach my coaching clients, with copy and paste message examples you can use today.


What you'll learn in this video:
- The 6-step networking system that generates job interviews on demand
- Exactly who to message, and the one group of people you are wasting your time on
- The real reply rates for alumni, peers, and hiring managers, so you contact the right people first
- The 4-part cold message that gets replies, with a full copy and paste example
- The Impact Loop that turns a single reply into a referral and an interview


VIDEO CHAPTERS:
0:00 The message that gets you interviews
0:49 Step 1: who to actually message

transcript: I'm going to give you the exact six-step networking system that gets my candidates job interviews without sending a single extra application. And the message on your screen right now is the kind of thing it gets you. It's a reply from inside the company that turns into an interview. Now, the candidate that got that landed six interviews in one single month. He didn't get a better CV than anyone else. He he didn't have more experience. The only thing that he changed about his approach was who he messaged and then what he actually said. because almost everyone networks in the way that just guarantees to get you ignored. What they do is they send some kind of version of, "Hi, you know, my name is X. I'd love to pick your brain. Have you got 20 minutes?" And this gets ignored every single time because that message is all about taking and there's no give. And you're asking a stranger for their time before you've actually given them any sort of reason to really care about you. So, this system does the complete opposite. Step one is the part that everyone gets wrong, which is who you actually message. So, when most people decide to network, they they just go straight into recruiters or HR and they're just asking what roles are open. And I I kind of get why because it feels like the most direct line to an actual job, but it's the worst use of your time. You know, recruiters, they get hammered day after day with those messages all day, and they're not the people who will sort of champion you throughout the actual process and throughout the building of the company. And this matters way more than almost anything else that you do because 72% of the jobs get filled through referrals and internal networks and only 28% come off the job boards directly. So the people already inside your target companies that you want to work for are the door to nearly 3/4 of the roles out there on the job market. So the people that you actually want are the ones doing the job you actually want or sitting one level above it. So, right at the top of your list is anyone that you share something real with, like the same old employer, the same hometown, the same university, like alumni. From the messages my candidates send, these people reply about 30 to 40% of the time because that shared thing makes you a real person instead of just a random stranger. Now, next is people currently doing your target role. So, basically, your future peers. Now, they reply about 15 to 20% of the time and they're gold because they know exactly what the team is looking for. And then the hiring managers or one level above the role. So the reply rate is lower. It's around 10 to 15%. But if you build a relationship with one of them before a job is even posted, you're already in their head the moment that that kind of job opens up. And here's the rule that I give every single candidate of mine. Don't message 10 people at one company. You need to message two or three people each like across as many companies as you can and only apply to one role per company. So the whole point of these messages isn't to beg for a job. It's to gather ammunition for a genuinely strong application and future interviews. So, your default from now on is that you already know someone inside a company before you ever apply. So, we've covered like who you should message. Now, step two is like what you'd actually say to those people. And this is where it kind of falls apart for most people networking. So, effectively, your first message has one job. It's not to get a call. It's not to get some referral or a cheap CV review. Is to just get a reply. So everything about it should make replying as easy as humanly possible. So the biggest mistake is leading with yourself. So I see it all the time. People open up with, "Hi, I'm this person. I'm a candidate looking for this type of role." And the person reading it kind of switches off instantly because it's all about you and there's nothing really in it for them. So you need to flip it completely. You need to open with something specific about them. Something like, "Hi Rachel. I noticed that you also moved from operations into product." and that it means it's about her and it proves you actually looked at her profile instead of just blasting the same line to a hundred different people. Then the one line on who you are just enough just to place you so they know who you are. And then you ask and this is the one you've got to actually get right. And it has to be specific and it has to be a small ask. So never ask on the first message, oh can we hop on a call for 30 minutes? And don't ask for things like can you refer me because those are massive asks from a total stranger. Instead, you have to ask for something that they can answer in a sentence or ideally one or two words. So something like, "If you had to choose between Python or SQL to be best at data analytics, which one would you pick?" And then you make it easy to say no with something like, "No worries at all if you're busy." And that one line actually lifts your reply rate because it takes the pressure off them to reply. So if you put it all together, it would sound something like this. Hi Rachel, I noticed that you also moved from operations into product, which is the exact jump that I'm trying to make as well. If you had to point to one thing that made it click, what was it? And then you sign off with your name, best and then in my case, Oliver. And altogether, that's about 50 words. And it's about her. And it gives her a reason to like you before you've asked for anything real. Because every relationship has some kind of karma tank. Every time you ask for something, you take a little bit out. And you can't make a withdrawal before you've actually put something in. So make sure you do the work and the homework first. Now, if they don't reply, that doesn't mean that it's a no. Most people, they're just busy or they barely open LinkedIn, for example. So, it's completely fine to follow up two or three times before you then move on. Now, let's get to the point where they reply. So, step three is to ask for one small favor. And this is where most people blow it. What they do is they get a helpful reply and then immediately go, "Amazing. Thanks. Any chance you could refer me or jump on a call?" And then just like that, the conversation goes cold because the person feels like you didn't even read their reply. You didn't acknowledge their advice. You just wanted something from them. Now, I had a candidate do exactly this. He got a detailed, generous reply, went straight in for the 20-minut call, and the guy just went. So, what you need to do is the opposite. You ask for one tiny small favor. Something really simple. It's not a job. It's just a it's just a piece of advice. Something like, you know, what would you focus on first if you were in my position? It's small and it's flattering and it gives them an easy way to actually help you. Now, step four is the one that almost nobody does and it's the one that changes absolutely everything in networking. So whatever they told you to do, you need to go and actually do it. And so if they said like get your hands on a certain tool, for example, you need to spend the weekend building something small with it. If they said read a certain report or a book, you read it and form a real opinion. So make sure you take the advice and then you actually run with it. Now that's kind of the easy bit because then in step five, about a week later, you then come back and then you show what you actually did. So it would sound something like this. So hey Rachel, you told me to get hands- on with that analytics tool before applying. So I spent the weekend building a small project with it and here's what I found. and then you'd have some sort of small acknowledgement to say thank you. Now, most people would never come back to that. So, when you do and you show them that you genuinely listened and acted on it, you completely stand out because people love feeling like they actually help someone who actually runs with it and puts their money where their mouth is. So, those three steps, the small favor, the action, and then the report back. That's what I call the impact loop. And it's the thing that quietly builds that real trust with someone who actually started out as just a complete stranger. And that then develops into step six, which is where it all kind of pays off. So you let the referral come to you. Now, when the role opens up on their team, you're not a stranger asking for some sort of favor anymore. You're the person who took their advice and actually ran with it. So the referral becomes their idea, not just your ask. And they're more likely to put your name forward. And that's the message that you saw at the very start. And there's also a second payoff that most people miss. So everything they tell you in those conversations like the tools the team actually uses, how they work, what they really care about, all of that is ammunition. So when the interview comes up and they ask, you know, why this company, you're the only candidate in the entire pool in the room who can answer it with something real because you actually spoke to someone on the inside. Now, you don't earn that kind of trust by asking for it. You have to build it by showing up and proving you'll act. And that's how a cold message turns into an interview. And this is exactly what Ella Moran did. So he was 21, he didn't have a degree and he was working as an apprentice and he was earning £27,000 a year. And the thing that frustrated with him is that he didn't get a raise. So what he did is he ran this system. He messaged the right people the right way and it lined him up for six interviews in a single month. He treated the first few as practice, acted on the feedback, and after each one, it turned into a £58,000 offer. And that is 110% pay rise. So the networking alone got him in the room and then he gave them every reason to say yes. So that is the whole system. So you message people and the right people. You make the first message about them with one tiny ask. You then ask for a small favor. You act on it. You report back and then you let the referral come to you. If you do that and you're going to stop waiting around on job boards and start generating interviews on demand. title: If You Don't Understand Recruiter Search, You Don't Understand LinkedIn
description:
If You Don't Understand Recruiter Search, You Don't Understand LinkedIn

FREE GUIDE:
My LinkedIn guide walks every section of your profile that a recruiter search reads. Headline formula, about, experience, skills, featured, and the Open to Work setting that actually matters.
https://offeraccelerator.co.uk/join-free-training-organic?source=youtube&utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=description&utm_campaign=recruiter-search-101


CONNECT WITH ME
LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/olivercordingley
Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/o.cordingley


WATCH NEXT:
4 LinkedIn Changes That Got Me 19 Recruiter Messages (No Applications)

Most people optimise LinkedIn as if a recruiter reads profiles one by one. They don't. They begin with a search, and if your job title, skills, location and evidence do not fit that search, the rest of your profile may never matter.

This video builds a recruiter search from a real UK job brief. You will watch a financial analyst vacancy in London get stripped down to 3 searchable fields, see the 2 filters recruiters add that are not on the brief at all, watch a genuinely qualified candidate disappear out of the results, and get the 5 checks that make your profile easier to find.


What you'll learn in this video:
- How a 700 word job advert becomes the 3 fields a LinkedIn recruiter actually searches
- The 2 extra filters recruiters add themselves that are on no job brief anywhere
- Why 3 companies give the same job 3 different titles, and how to pick your 1
- The 3 ways a qualified candidate disappears from recruiter search results
- The 4 places your job title needs evidence behind it before a recruiter believes it


VIDEO CHAPTERS:
0:00 How recruiters actually start
0:27 The job brief, and what survives it
2:09 Filter 1, the job title
2:40 Adjacent titles, one job under 3 names
3:17 Filter 2, the city, never the country
3:52 Filter 3, the skills in the advert's own words
4:56 Filters 4 and 5, activity and open to work
6:00 Running the search
6:18 The candidate who should be there and isn't
6:53 The 3 ways to disappear
8:02 Three companies, three names for one job
11:08 The evidence layer, 4 places to prove it
13:31 The 5 checks to run tonight


Work through all 5 checks with the wording in front of you.


ABOUT ME:
I dropped out of university at 19 to build recruitment software and ATS systems used by hiring teams. For years I spoke to hundreds of hiring managers and recruiters every day, learning exactly how candidates get filtered, shortlisted, and hired from the inside. I started coaching friends through their job search using what I'd seen, then raised investment, built a software company, and hired my own team. I've seen hiring from every angle.

Today I help job seekers land offers faster using a proven 3-step system. I've coached hundreds of candidates into roles at firms like JP Morgan, Goldman Sachs, Deloitte, EY, and PwC and many more.

title: Every Way to Find a Job in the UK, Ranked Worst to Best
description:
Every Way to Find a Job in the UK, Ranked Worst to Best


If you are stuck in the UK job search, firing off LinkedIn Easy Apply and Indeed applications and hearing nothing back, you are probably spending 90% of your time on one of the worst methods there is. In this video I rank every realistic way to find a job in the UK from worst to best, and show you why they all really come down to one thing: how warm you get before you apply.

Roughly 70% of jobs are never posted publicly. They get filled through referrals, internal networks and direct outreach before they ever reach a job board. These are the job search strategies that actually move you up the ranking, whether you are a career changer, a recent leaver, or just not getting interviews from the big boards.


What you'll learn in this video:
- Why auto apply bots and mass applying convert at just 1 to 3% and get you filtered out
- The applicant tracking system search trick that surfaces live roles days before the big boards
- How to make recruiters find you on LinkedIn by fixing one thing in your profile
- The 2 minute hiring manager outreach that gets 3 to 5 times the interview rate
- Why a referred candidate converts at 15 to 30% and how to get warm before you apply


VIDEO CHAPTERS:
0:00 The most popular way to find a job is the worst
0:33 Why this is one ranking, not seven methods
0:55 No. 7: Auto apply bots and Easy Apply spraying
1:04 No. 6: Mass applying on the big job boards
1:44 How Arun went from no replies to an offer in 3 weeks
2:08 No. 5: Recruiters and recruitment agencies
2:54 No. 4: Careers pages, niche boards and the ATS search trick
3:40 No. 3: Getting recruiters to find you on LinkedIn
4:29 No. 2: Direct outreach to the hiring manager
5:32 No. 1: The hidden job market and warm referrals
6:29 Who to actually contact and how to follow up
6:55 The one pattern behind the whole ranking


Most people pour all of their energy into the very bottom of this list and wonder why nothing comes back. If you want to climb it, this is where I would start.

WORK WITH ME:
Join my free community for the full job search system, the outreach templates, and the exact way to get warm before you apply:
https://community.offeraccelerator.co.uk/join?invitation_token=f1eaf2eb4891316c06b827f77255cb8b209dd952-daae48f6-0b4f-44fe-833a-04e7c487467c&utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=description&utm_campaign=every-way-find-job-uk-ranked


CONNECT WITH ME
LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/olivercordingley
Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/olivercordingley


WATCH NEXT:
1 In 3 Jobs You Apply To Are Ghost Jobs


ABOUT ME:
I dropped out of university at 19 to build recruitment software and ATS systems used by hiring teams. For years I spoke to hundreds of hiring managers and recruiters every day, learning exactly how candidates get filtered, shortlisted, and hired from the inside. I started coaching friends through their job search using what I'd seen, then raised investment, built a software company, and hired my own team. I've seen hiring from every angle.

Today I help job seekers land offers faster using a proven 3-step system. I've coached hundreds of candidates into roles at firms like JP Morgan, Goldman Sachs, Deloitte, EY, and PwC and many more.

title: Why Recruiters Skip Your CV in Seconds (39,184 CVs Analysed)
description:
Why Recruiters Skip Your CV in Seconds (39,184 CVs Analysed)

FREE GUIDE:
My free CV Guide has the CV template plus the exact ChatGPT prompt series for tailoring it to any job description.
https://offeraccelerator.co.uk/join-free-training-organic?source=youtube&utm_medium=description&utm_campaign=why-recruiters-skip-your-cv


CONNECT WITH ME
LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/olivercordingley
Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/o.cordingley


WATCH NEXT:
ATS Isn't Rejecting Your CV. This Is. (3 Real Filters)
https://youtu.be/lhxQi9nupHU?si=3GCqLtMiNlwBR8pY

A study of 39,184 CVs compared which ones led to an interview and which ones were ignored. This video walks through what that research actually measured, the CV findings that change your interview rate, and what happens in the 6 to 10 seconds a recruiter spends on your CV on the first pass, which is a separate thing the study never tracked.

If your CV is getting rejected and you have been rewriting it for every application without getting interviews, this is the evidence base to work from.


What you'll learn in this video:
- What the 39,184 CV study measured, its 3 limits, and the claims it does not support
- Why tailoring doubled the interview rate, 4.23% against 2.07%
- Why the one page CV rule is dead, 2 pages interviewed at 7.40% against 5.01%
- The F shaped scan pattern and the 3 things that pull a recruiter's eye in the first 6 to 10 seconds
- Why an ATS score is a number no employer ever sees, and what knockout questions really filter


VIDEO CHAPTERS:
0:00 Why recruiters skip a CV in seconds
0:40 The source, the sample, and the method
2:30 What the study never measured
0:54 Tailoring, 4.23% against 2.07%
1:08 A hard number in your summary
1:24 CV length and bullet depth
1:52 Averages are not rules, and the 2 to 4 year trough
3:11 The 6 to 10 second scan and the F pattern
3:49 The 3 things that pull a recruiter's eye
4:36 The ATS myth and knockout questions
5:46 One role, one CV, and visible proof
6:51 The before and after bullet rewrite
8:13 The 5 point second look check


Run the 5 point check on your own CV, and use my template and prompts to fix what it turns up.

ABOUT ME:
I dropped out of university at 19 to build recruitment software and ATS systems used by hiring teams. For years I spoke to hundreds of hiring managers and recruiters every day, learning exactly how candidates get filtered, shortlisted, and hired from the inside. I started coaching friends through their job search using what I'd seen, then raised investment, built a software company, and hired my own team. I've seen hiring from every angle.

Today I help job seekers land offers faster using a proven 3-step system. I've coached hundreds of candidates into roles at firms like JP Morgan, Goldman Sachs, Deloitte, EY, and PwC and many more.

of experience? Do you hold a certain
certification?" So, when you make an
application and one of those answers is
wrong based on your CV, then you will be
filtered out before anybody opens your
CV. So, there are three separate stages
and people sort of collapse them into
one. So, the form knocks you out, the
system then passes and ranks you, and
then a human scans it. So, that's how a
CV is processed. And that is why a tool
selling you an ATS score is selling you
a number that no employer ever sees.
It's not even relevant to the
recruitment space. There is no such
thing as an ATS score. So, here's how as
a candidate I would use all of this
information to my advantage. So, the
first thing is pick one target role and
build one CV for it. So, don't go and
create 20 almost identical versions
aimed at 20 different job titles because
the moment you spread across 20 titles,
you just look like everybody else trying
to apply and you're not being consistent
and then you can't then defend yourself
in an interview. Then, the second thing
is you need to position it. So, the job
title at the top of your CV should match
the title on the advert. Now, if you
don't feel comfortable writing that
title, that's probably a sign that
you're applying to the wrong role
anyway. Then, you need to make your
proof visible and visible means in that
top third and down the left-hand side.
So, a number buried in the last bullet
of page two, it you know, it might as
well not exist. It's not going to be
seen. And also like if you're in that
two to four year experience band, you
need to be honest with yourself about
what the CV can do because your CV is
being compared, it's getting read next
to people with probably two to three
times your experience. So, making it
better raises a ceiling that was kind of
low to start with, which is why
candidates that I work with spend less
time on the CV than they actually expect
to and far more on which roles they
should go after and then who they know
inside those companies. So, let me show
you what that looks like on sort of
like, you know, a real example. So, say
the job advert asked for experience with
stakeholder management across, you know,
cross-functional teams and your bullet
currently reads led the quarterly
project review with engineering,
marketing and operations teams. That is
a decent bullet, but it's just not
written in their words. So, the
recruiter has to translate it and in
that six-second scan, they probably
won't bother. So, you rewrite it as
something like this. Led quarterly
stakeholder management across
cross-functional teams in engineering,
marketing and operations cutting review
time by 30%. So, that is the exact same
work and experience and you've matched
their language and you've added the
number that catches the eye and then you
move that bullet into the top of that
role so that it lands in that zone that
actually gets scanned. Now, if you're
not sure about where your CV stands at
the moment, here's sort of like a second
look check. So, I'm going to talk you
through five things and every one of
them is something the evidence actually
supports. So, the first thing is you
need to pull up the last job description
you applied to and see if you can find
five phrases from that advert inside
your CV, just in your own true
sentences. The second thing is then look
at the job title at the top of your CV
and ask whether it's the title on the
advert or like maybe one step under it.
Now, the third thing is then find the
top third of your page one on the CV and
check there's at least one hard number
and one recognizable name sitting in it.
Now, the fourth thing is then count
those bullets in your most recent role.
If there are sort of like two or three
then you're under the average. What you
want is sort of that three to five range
and and everyone needs at least a result
in it. And then the fifth and final
thing is then go back to the application
form questions, not the CV, and then
work out whether you actually met every
hard requirement. And that's the one
stage that could automatically reject
you. So, the real lesson from that
39,000 plus CV study isn't some sort of
magic template or a fake ATS score, is
making sure that your CV survives all
three of those stages that I've just
walked you through. So, if you want the
template and the exact prompt series
that I use to do all of that against the
job description, my free CV guide is
linked in the description. It's got the
CV template itself plus the prompts for
tailoring it to any advert. So, go and
grab that and then run the five-point
check before you send the next one.

title: Why You Get The Interview But Not The Job (And How To Fix It)
description:
Interviews But No Offers? | The Real Reason You Get Rejected


You keep getting the interviews, and then a week later the rejection email lands. It's rarely your experience, your CV already proved that, and that's why you got the interview in the first place. In this video I break down the real reason you get interviews but no offers, and the 3 shifts that turn a final round interview into an actual job offer.

A company's interview process comes in 2 halves. The early rounds screen whether you can do the job. The final interview is almost always about positioning and trust, whether they can actually picture working with you, and that is where most candidates lose the offer. This is how to win it.


What you'll learn in this video:
- Why you keep getting interviews but no job offers, and why it has almost nothing to do with your experience
- Why a company's interview process comes in 2 halves, and why the final interview is decided on trust, not skill
- The difference between reciting and storytelling in a job interview, and why storytelling is what wins offers
- How to answer behavioural interview questions with a simple story structure, and why you lead with the result
- How to answer "why do you want to work here" so you do not sound like every other candidate


VIDEO CHAPTERS:
0:00 Interviews but no offers
0:37 The one thing Elamaran changed
0:49 Why interview processes come in 2 halves
1:33 The final interview is about trust, not skill
2:31 Shift 1: Stop reciting, start telling stories
3:41 Lead with the result
4:31 Shift 2: The 4 things they actually judge
5:14 The answer that wins on culture fit
6:14 Shift 3: The delivery they remember
8:32 What to do before your next interview


Stop preparing for the interview like it is an exam and start preparing to build trust. Here is how I can help:

WORK WITH ME:
The Offer Accelerator is my full system for landing offers faster. Personal brand, CV, LinkedIn, networking, applications, interviews, the lot.
https://community.offeraccelerator.co.uk/join?invitation_token=f1eaf2eb4891316c06b827f77255cb8b209dd952-daae48f6-0b4f-44fe-833a-04e7c487467c&utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=description&utm_campaign=interviews-but-no-offers


CONNECT WITH ME
LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/olivercordingley
Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/olivercordingley


WATCH NEXT:
The Interview Question That Costs You The Job


ABOUT ME:
I dropped out of university at 19 to build recruitment software and ATS systems used by hiring teams. For years I spoke to hundreds of hiring managers and recruiters every day, learning exactly how candidates get filtered, shortlisted, and hired from the inside. I started coaching friends through their job search using what I'd seen, then raised investment, built a software company, and hired my own team. I've seen hiring from every angle.

Today I help job seekers land offers faster using a proven 3-step system. I've coached hundreds of candidates into roles at firms like JP Morgan, Goldman Sachs, Deloitte, EY, and PwC and many more.


#jobsearch #careeradvice #interview
transcript: Elemeran sat through four final round interviews and got rejected from three of them before he got the offer. Now, there was nothing that he changed on his CV or his experience. He was the same background that got him into the room in the first place. And then what he did is he changed one thing about the way he answered, and then that fourth interview turned into that offer and a job that almost doubled his salary from 27,500 to 58,000 pounds. So, if you keep getting those interviews and then a week later the rejection email lands, you need to watch this because the reason you're not getting that offer has almost nothing to do with your experience. Your CV has already proved your experience already, and that's literally why you're in the room in the first place. And what Elemeran did is he didn't change his CV or his experience. He stopped reciting his answers and he started to build trust. And to understand the why that flipped everything, you need to see how these interview processes are actually built. So, a company's interview process comes in two halves. So, the first few rounds, the online test, you know, the numerical reasonings, that first technical interview, they're all there to check one thing. And it's basically, can you do the job? skill screen and it's tangible and it's about ability and and competency. And it's basically a pass or fail. But here's the part that almost nobody realizes. By the time that you reach that final stage interview, you've already passed all of that. So, if you're four or five rounds deep, think about how much time that whole team has already put into you. They decided that you're good enough on paper. They've qualified your ability. So, that final interview is almost never about whether you can actually do the job. It's purely an emotional decision. And the real question in the room is, can I actually work with this person, you know, 40 hours a week for the next few years? And that's the exact bit that you keep losing on. So, it's not your ability, it's your positioning and it's the trust that you build in that interview room. Because most candidates they walk into that final interview still just trying to prove that they're competent when when competence was settled, you know, two or three rounds ago. And what they do is they keep showing up as a candidate and then the offer goes to the person who shows up like a colleague. So, you need to think about it from the other side of the table. So, the employer they've probably got three or four people left who, you know, they can all do the job. And on paper, there's barely anything different between them. So, it doesn't really come down to who's the most qualified. It comes down to who they trust and who they've warmed to and who they actually picture on their team. So, when you recite your interview answers, none of that lands and when you tell a story, all of it does. So, let me show you the three shifts that turn that final round interview from a rejection into an offer. And every one of them is really about the same thing. It's building that trust and getting them to see you as a colleague instead of a candidate. So, let's start with the first because this one is where most people go wrong. So, the first shift is you need to stop reciting and you need to start telling stories. Now, here's what reciting actually sounds like. You know, someone asked you to tell them a time about when you, you know, solved a problem and then you go into this polished paragraph, probably using the STAR or CAR method, that you've clearly said out loud, probably 40 times in the mirror before that interview. And probably on paper, it's probably word perfect, but it's completely forgettable. So, then the interviewer's attention just drifts off somewhere and then they're probably just waiting for you to stop. Whereas a story is a completely different thing. A story has a scene, a problem, what you actually did and how it turned out. And it's the exact same shape that you, you know, when you tell a story to your friends or your family or around dinner, for example. You set the scene, something goes wrong, you deal with it and then there's something that happened. You don't need a fancy method or some five-letter acronym for this. You just need to talk like a human being who was actually there. And before we even get into the story, watch how you start it. Because most people, what they do is they spend the first 30 seconds explaining the company, the team, the whole background before they even get anywhere near the actual situation. And by the time they reach that point, the interviewer's attention's gone. So, set the scene in a sentence or two and then get straight into the meat of your answer. And here's the one tweak that also makes a massive difference. You need to lead with the result. So, most candidates who come to me after they've been rejected, what they do is they save the outcome to the very end. So, then the interviewer has to sit through two minutes of build-up before they find out why the story even mattered. So, what you need to do is flip it on its head. So, a candidate that I worked with used to bury his first number right at the end of every answer. And what we did is we changed it, and he started opening with something like this. I made a change that saved business around 4 million, and here's how I did it. Now, the interviewer is leaning in for the whole story instead of just waiting around for the whole point. And then also, just keep it to one story. So, give them a problem, give them an outcome, and then stop. The moment you say, "Oh, also, another time I did this," you've lost them because now they're half listening to you and then half trying to work out what actually happened. So, one clean story for every question you get, about 60 to 90 seconds, and then stop talking. Now, the second shift is being specific about what the final interview is really judging you on because you have to remember it's not your competence anymore. That's already been banked, it's been assessed. It's the emotional stuff, and there's four things that are sitting underneath all of it, and it's your motivation, whether you're a fit for the culture, your potential, and then how you professionally carry yourself. And that motivation and culture fit are where most offers are won or lost. So, let me give you the one that just quietly cost most people their offers, and it's that culture fit. Now, having spoken to hundreds of hiring managers, they always say that they would pick someone less qualified who feels like they're a better fit over the more qualified person who feels hard to work with, and it's almost every single time it's like that. So, they're not just hiring on skill set. What they're doing is they're choosing someone that they've got to sit next to every day for the next few years. That's what they're preparing to do. So, the type of questions that you'll get asked to assess this are things like, you know, why do you want to work here? And most people, what they do is they answer something like this. "Oh, I love what you do. I'm really passionate about the industry." It tells them nothing, and it sounds exactly like every other candidate on that day. So, the fix is to get specific and make it personal. So, what you need to do is reference one real thing about them, and then say why it actually matters to you. And then the strongest version of all of this is when you can say that you've actually spoken to someone who actually works at the company. So, a candidate I worked with messaged a the on the sales team a few days before this interview, and he just had a quick chat. And then in the room in that interview, he could say, "Oh, yeah, I spoke to Jack on your team. He told me about how you run sprints." And honestly, that's the kind of environment that I do my best work in. Now, that's not something that you can just fake or memorize off a website or what other candidates do. It proves your motivation and that culture fit in a single sentence. It's the kind of thing that quietly wins those offers. Then the third shift is one that actually nobody prepares for, and it's the delivery. So, when I talk to hiring managers and interviewers, most of them they can't really remember the specific words that, you know, a candidate said in the interview. What they remember is the feeling that they left with. Like, did this person feel sharp or warm or, you know, easy to work with? And that feeling is what walks into the room when they sit down and they decide as a committee. And you could be the most qualified person in the process and still lose on that feeling. And this matters even more on a video interview because you have to remember your energy just gets flattened through a screen. So, that thing that feels like normal enthusiasm to you comes across as a bit flat on camera. So, you actually have to put in a bit more into it that feels natural and just to make it land more normally. Now, here's where most people sabotage their own delivery. What they do, and I see it time and time again, they memorize their answers word for word. And memorizing is the most fragile thing you can do because the second that you get a question in a slightly different shape than you practiced, the whole script falls apart and then you freeze. And the fix isn't just to memorize harder, it's to stop writing your answers out. And you need to start saying them out loud. Literally, record yourself telling the story on a voice note, in the car, like on a walk, until the shape of it just feels natural. And then the words come out fresh and you feel comfortable about it. Then what you do is you rehearse the structure. So, you don't rehearse the exact words. Now, if you're nervous in the interview, you're honestly allowed to just say it. Something like, "I'll be honest with you. I'm a little bit nervous because I really want this one." And a decent interviewer warms to that straight away because it's honest and it tells them that you care. And it also it will calm you down because you've already said it out loud. Because the reality is the nerves in the interview room are never the problem. It's always just trying to hide it because it builds pressure on you and then you start to forget. So, going back to Elon Musk for a second, like nothing about his CV changed across those four final interviews. What changed is that he realized the final rounds weren't testing whether he could do the job. He knew that they already decided it. They were testing whether they could trust him, whether they could actually picture working with him. So, by the fourth one, he stopped showing up as a candidate trying to prove himself all the time. He started showing up like a future colleague. So, what he did is he told stories. He built trust and that interview turned into an offer that doubled his salary. And remember, he was exactly the same on paper. All of it changed just on how he communicated it. So, before your next interview, you need to do this. Take three or four of your best stories, the ones that you, you know, genuinely proud of, and then practice them out loud as stories, not scripts. Lead with the result, cut the second example, and prepare one real reason you want to work at that company. And ideally, from actually talking to someone who works there already. So, if you want the full breakdown of all of this, you know, the exact story structures, you know, the questions that catch people out, I'm going to go through all of this inside the Offer Accelerator and the link is in the description below if you want to join. And I promise you, if you get this right and you master storytelling, you're going to stop walking in as a candidate that they're judging and you're going to start walking in as a colleague that they really want and that is where you get the attractive offers.

title: Why You're Failing Assessment Centres (And How To Fix It)
description:
You're Solving The Wrong Test | How To Pass An Assessment Centre


Most people fail an assessment centre for one reason: they treat it as a test to solve, when it is a full day of your behaviour being observed and scored. If you keep reaching the assessment centre or the final-stage day and getting rejected, this video breaks down what assessors are actually marking and exactly how to pass an assessment centre.

You'll get the assessment centre group exercise strategy that gets you noticed for the right reasons, how to handle the case study and presentation so they score your thinking, and the prep that kills the nerves before you walk in.


What you'll learn in this video:
- Why competence is already screened before the assessment centre, and what assessors actually score on the day
- The exact assessment centre group exercise strategy: how to lead without dominating or disappearing
- The 5 behaviours on the assessor's scorecard, and how to hit each one
- How to handle the case study and presentation so they mark your thinking, not just your answer
- The prep that removes the unknowns, straight from the recruiter and Glassdoor, before you walk in


VIDEO CHAPTERS:
0:00 The real reason smart candidates fail
0:54 What an assessment centre actually scores
1:53 Shift 1: kill the unknowns before you walk in
2:26 Prep the format from the recruiter and Glassdoor
3:13 Shift 2: the group exercise most people lose
4:00 The dominate or disappear trap
4:25 How to lead the group without dominating
5:09 Shift 3: the case study and presentation
5:24 Why they score your thinking, not your answer
6:27 Cut your slides to one point
6:54 The whole day is the assessment
7:35 What to fix first


You don't pass an assessment centre by being the smartest person in the room. You pass it by fixing what is actually costing you points. Here's where to start:

The Online Tests Rejecting You (Before Any Interview)


ABOUT ME:
I dropped out of university to build recruitment software and ATS systems used by hiring teams. For years I spoke to hundreds of hiring managers and recruiters every day, learning exactly how candidates get filtered, shortlisted, and hired from the inside. I started coaching friends through their job search using what I'd seen, then raised investment, built a software company, and hired my own team. I've seen hiring from every angle.

Today I help job seekers land offers faster using a proven 3-step system. I've coached hundreds of candidates into roles at firms like JP Morgan, Goldman Sachs, Deloitte, EY, and PwC and many more.

title: Why Most Candidates Fail Numerical Reasoning (And How You Won't)
description:
This Test Rejects You In 20 Minutes | Pass Numerical & Verbal Reasoning


Most candidates get auto-rejected by a numerical reasoning test or a verbal reasoning test before a single human reads their CV, and they never find out it happened. This online assessment is usually the highest-elimination round in the whole hiring process, and at a lot of employers, failing it locks you out from reapplying for a year. This video shows you exactly how to pass numerical and verbal reasoning tests, the specific traps that fail most people, and how to prepare so the timer never beats you.

Whether your aptitude test comes from SHL, Korn Ferry, cut-e or Talent Q, the mechanics are the same, and they are beatable once you know what each one is actually measuring.


What you'll learn in this video:
- Why a 20-minute online assessment rejects more candidates than any interview stage
- How to find out exactly which test and provider you are sitting before you practise
- The units trap that fails candidates who got the numerical reasoning maths right
- The one discipline that decides every verbal reasoning test (true, false, cannot say)
- How to practise aptitude tests the right way, and when guessing helps or costs you marks


VIDEO CHAPTERS:
0:00 The test that rejected him in 20 minutes
0:57 Find out exactly which test you are sitting
2:00 Numerical reasoning and the units trap
3:09 Stop estimating, work the actual sum
3:29 How to pace each question
3:48 Verbal reasoning: answer only from the passage
4:24 The qualifier trap, all versus some
5:00 False versus cannot say
5:18 Practise the format, not the answers
5:57 When to guess and when not to
6:21 Your environment is part of the test
6:36 What to fix first


The test is only one filter. If you keep getting knocked out and cannot tell where, start here.

FREE DIAGNOSIS:
Take the free 2-minute diagnosis. Get your personalised employability score plus a roadmap of exactly what to fix first in your job search.
https://the.offeraccelerator.uk/new-candidate-diagnosis?source=youtube&utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=description&utm_campaign=pass-numerical-verbal-reasoning-tests

LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/olivercordingley

AI is already rejecting your job application


ABOUT ME:
I dropped out of university at 19 to build recruitment software and ATS systems used by hiring teams. For years I spoke to hundreds of hiring managers and recruiters every day, learning exactly how candidates get filtered, shortlisted, and hired from the inside. I started coaching friends through their job search using what I'd seen, then raised investment, built a software company, and hired my own team. I've seen hiring from every angle.

Today I help job seekers land offers faster using a proven 3-step system. I've coached hundreds of candidates into roles at firms like JP Morgan, Goldman Sachs, Deloitte, EY, and PwC and many more.

For most candidates, this is the single highest elimination round in the entire process, and they never find out what's actually the reason for keep getting them rejected. But here's what actually knocked and it's the same thing knocking you out. It isn't that you wasn't clever enough. These tests don't measure how clever you are. They measure whether you know the format and whether you avoid these three specific traps. So, not checking the units on a numerical chart, answering verbal question from your own knowledge instead of actually what's given you, and practicing the wrong test completely. And those three fail more candidates than anything else. So, let's fix all three and we'll start with the one that decides whether your practice even counts. So, that first one is finding out exactly which test and which provider you're actually sitting before you practice a single question. This is the step that almost everyone skips and it's the step that makes all your practice count because a numerical test from one provider looks and behaves nothing like another one. And if you practice the wrong version, you've prepared hard for a test that you're not even going to sit. So, there are three main ways to find out. The invitation email usually names the provider, so read it properly instead of just clicking the link. If it doesn't say, just ask the recruiter or hiring manager and they'll normally tell you. And if neither of those work, search the company name together with the word assessment because other candidates have almost always been through it and they've documented and described the exact format online. So, 10 minutes of doing that is worth far more than 10 hours of just random practice. And I'm not guessing any of this. Like I've spent years building recruitment software and sat on the other side of the hiring desk. And I've watched which filters actually knock people out and this early test is one of the biggest because it runs automatically before anyone of the team has actually looked at your profile. So, let's go through the two tests. You got the numerical first. So, So, with numerical reasoning, you get a table or a chart and you have to pull the right number out and do something with it. So, that's usually a percentage, a ratio, or a change over time. It's not advanced math. It's probably GCSE level maths under a stopwatch time pressure, which means that the maths is almost never what beats you. It's these two specific things. So, the first one is the units. So, the chart is in thousands and then the answer options are like in millions and you pick the number that looks right and it's wrong by a factor of a thousand. So, let me show you exactly how this happens. The chart shows revenue in thousands and then three regions sit at 250, 300, and 200. The question asks for a total revenue and the options are 750, 750,000, 7.5 million. Now, you add it up and you get 750, so you tick 750 and you've failed a question you actually got right. It's the same maths, but the chart was in thousands, so the real answer is 750,000. So, wrong units is the wrong answer and that's the whole test in one question. And the crazy part is this is the number one biggest reason why people fail numerical reasoning. So, before you calculate anything, read the axis, read the units, and read what the question is genuinely asking for. Now, the second thing is estimating. So, under time pressure, people eyeball the graph and just go, "Ah, that looks about right." and tick that. And the answer options are deliberately designed so that the rough answer and the exact answer are both sitting and sort of waiting for you side by side. So, you never estimate from a shape of a bar. You need to work the actual sum every time even when you think you can see it. And on the timing, most numerical tests give you about a minute or, you know, a minute and a half to actually answer per question. So, know your test exact ratio before you start. And if one question is eating your time, take your best worked answer and move on and that's important. Move on even if you feel like you've got it wrong cuz one hard question is never worth three easy ones that you just didn't get right. Now, the second test is the verbal reasoning. Here, you have a passage, then you get a statement, and then you have to say whether it's true, false, or you can't say based on only that passage. Now, there's one discipline that decides the entire test. You answer only from the passage, never from what you already know. So, if the passage doesn't give you enough to call something true or false, then you need to answer you cannot say, even when you happen to know the actual real answer out in the real world. And that one habit is basically the whole test. The people who fail verbal reasoning are almost always the people answering from their own general knowledge. Now, the second trap is the small words. So, the passage says most, and then the statement says all. So, the passage says usually, and then the statement says always. And that single word flips the entire answer. So, here's what that actually looks like. So, the passage says the company sales grew in most European markets last year. Then the statement says the company sales grew in all European markets. Your instinct is to tick true because it feels basically right, but most isn't all, and the passage never says all. So, the honest answer is you can't say. And the test is full of these, always one qualifier away from the answer you want to give. So, slow right down on the words like all, some, always, and never because the whole test is built around them. And when you're genuinely stuck between the false and cannot say, ask yourself one question. Does the passage actually contradict the statement, or does it just not mention it? If it contradicts it, it's obviously false. But if it doesn't cover it, it can't say it. And that one question clears up most of the ones you'd otherwise get wrong. So, those are the mechanics of both tests. The last piece is how you prepare, and this is where most people lose before you they even start it. They either don't practice at all, or they grind hundreds of random questions hoping to memorize their way through. And remember, none of that works. Practice isn't for memorizing answers because you'll genuinely probably never see the same question twice. It's for making the format familiar so that on the day, you know, you've got the timer, you don't panic, and you're not trying to learn sort of a new interface and answer the questions at the same time. title: Is Your CV Getting Rejected? 5 Mistakes You Must Fix
description:
The CV Mistakes That Get You Rejected in Seconds | 5 Fixes to Get Interviews


Recruiters spend about 7 seconds scanning your CV before they decide to bin it or keep reading, and most CVs get rejected on the same handful of mistakes. This video breaks down the 5 CV mistakes that get you rejected in seconds, and the exact fixes that get you interviews, from someone who built the recruitment software hiring teams use to filter candidates.

If you're sending applications and hearing nothing back, your CV is almost certainly making at least one of these 5 mistakes. Fix them and you'll get more out of your CV than another 100 applications ever would.


What you'll learn in this video:
- Why a human, not the ATS, rejects your CV in the first 7 seconds
- The what, how, why formula that turns weak bullet points into results, with real before and after examples
- Why a profile summary is wasting the most valuable space on your CV if you have under 10 years of experience
- The skills section and certification mistakes quietly lowering your interview rate
- How to tailor 1 strong CV per role and get interviews at more than double the rate, 4.23% vs 2.07%, from a study of 39,000 CVs


VIDEO CHAPTERS:
0:00 Why your CV gets rejected in 7 seconds
0:41 Mistake 1, bullet points with no results
1:00 The what, how, why bullet formula
3:02 Mistake 2, the profile summary killing your top third
4:22 Mistake 3, a skills section full of fluff
5:56 Mistake 4, the template that breaks the scan
7:01 Mistake 5, the same CV sent everywhere
7:25 Why tailoring doubles your interview rate
7:49 Your 5 fixes for this week
8:12 Find what's actually killing your CV


If you want to know exactly which of these is holding your CV back, here's where to start:

FREE DIAGNOSIS:
Take the free 2-minute diagnosis. Get your personalised employability score plus a roadmap of exactly what to fix first in your job search.
https://the.offeraccelerator.uk/new-candidate-diagnosis?source=youtube&utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=description&utm_campaign=cv-mistakes-rejected-in-seconds


CONNECT WITH ME
LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/olivercordingley
Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/olivercordingley


WATCH NEXT:
ATS Isn't Rejecting Your CV. This Is. (3 Real Filters)


ABOUT ME:
I dropped out of university at 19 to build recruitment software and ATS systems used by hiring teams. For years I spoke to hundreds of hiring managers and recruiters every day, learning exactly how candidates get filtered, shortlisted, and hired from the inside. I started coaching friends through their job search using what I'd seen, then raised investment, built a software company, and hired my own team. I've seen hiring from every angle.

Today I help job seekers land offers faster using a proven 3-step system. I've coached hundreds of candidates into roles at firms like JP Morgan, Goldman Sachs, Deloitte, EY, and PwC and many more.

title: How to Write a LinkedIn Headline That Recruiters Actually Search For
description:
Your LinkedIn Headline Is Making You Invisible


Your LinkedIn headline is the single line that decides whether recruiters ever find you, and for most job seekers it is quietly making them invisible in LinkedIn search. Recruiters do not scroll the feed. They use LinkedIn Recruiter like a search engine, typing a job title, a couple of skills and a location, then scanning each profile in about 6 to 10 seconds. If your headline says "aspiring" and "passionate about", you never show up.

This video breaks down how to write a good LinkedIn headline that actually gets you found, the 3-part headline formula that works for job seekers in any field, the words to delete today, and the one headline mistake that quietly caps your salary before you have even spoken to a recruiter.


What you'll learn in this video:
- How LinkedIn Recruiter actually searches for candidates, and why your headline carries the most weight
- The 3-part LinkedIn headline formula: target role, 2 to 4 searchable skills, and an impact line
- The exact words to delete from your headline today, starting with "aspiring"
- How to pull the right keywords for your headline from 5 real job adverts
- The junior-title mistake that caps your salary, and the location setting recruiters filter by

title: Tell Me About Yourself: Why You're Not Getting The Job
description:
They Don't Believe Your Tell Me About Yourself Answer


Tell me about yourself is the first question in almost every interview, and most candidates answer it by reading their CV back out loud. That is exactly why it lands flat. Your CV already told them what you are, so this question is the only part of the interview where they find out why you exist, and whether they believe you. This video breaks down why your tell me about yourself answer sounds like everybody else's, and the past, present, future story that fixes it.

It is for candidates who keep reaching interview and going no further, whose answers are all true but somehow never memorable. You will leave with a story you can actually say out loud, tested against the only thing that matters, which is whether someone could repeat it back.


What you'll learn in this video:
- Why your CV and your story do 2 completely different jobs, and why using the same words for both kills the answer
- The 90 second mistake: reading your CV back to someone who is already holding it
- Where your real reason actually starts, and why it is never your first proper job
- Why this is not a STAR answer, and the past, present, future structure to use instead
- The repeat back test that tells you whether you have a story or just a summary

title: You Need Sponsorship? Probably Not | Work In The UK Without Sponsorship
description:
You Need Sponsorship? Probably Not | Work In The UK Without Sponsorship


Thousands of international candidates get auto-rejected every year for visa sponsorship they don't actually need. If you are on a Graduate Visa, you have 2 years of unrestricted UK work rights with zero sponsorship required, and most hiring managers don't understand that. This video breaks down the sponsorship question on application forms, how to answer it, and the UK work visa routes that need no employer sponsor at all.

It is for international candidates and Graduate Visa holders who keep getting filtered out before a human reads their CV. You will leave knowing exactly how to stop self-rejecting and how to push back when a recruiter says "we can't sponsor".


What you'll learn in this video:
- Why the "do you need sponsorship" checkbox auto-rejects you before a human sees your CV
- What a UK Graduate Visa actually is: 2 years unrestricted work, zero employer cost
- The exact script to answer the sponsorship question on an application form
- A word-for-word message to push back when a recruiter says they can't sponsor
- 3 more UK work visa routes that need no employer sponsor (HPI, Global Talent, Youth Mobility)


VIDEO CHAPTERS:
0:00 You got rejected for sponsorship you didn't need
0:29 The application form trap
0:56 What a Graduate Visa actually is
1:24 What it costs the employer (nothing)
1:56 How to answer the sponsorship question
2:40 The exact pushback script for recruiters
3:10 What "we can't sponsor" really means
4:09 3 routes that need no sponsor at all
4:54 Check gov.uk for your route


If you want help positioning yourself so the visa stops ending your applications, come and join us.

WORK WITH ME:
Join my free community: https://community.offeraccelerator.co.uk/join?invitation_token=31dd2c6ff3c2d29110be25aace66bb325cab07f2-68a0b5d6-d377-438f-bb72-6e0ede239116&utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=description&utm_campaign=stop-saying-you-need-sponsorship


CONNECT WITH ME
LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/olivercordingley
Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/olivercordingley


WATCH NEXT:
Your CV is Why You're Not Getting Hired


ABOUT ME:
I dropped out of university at 19 to build recruitment software and ATS systems used by hiring teams. For years I spoke to hundreds of hiring managers and recruiters every day, learning exactly how candidates get filtered, shortlisted, and hired from the inside. I started coaching friends through their job search using what I'd seen, then raised investment, built a software company, and hired my own team. I've seen hiring from every angle.

Today I help job seekers land offers faster using a proven 3-step system. I've coached hundreds of candidates into roles at firms like JP Morgan, Goldman Sachs, Deloitte, EY, and PwC and many more.

title: 4 LinkedIn Changes That Got Me 19 Recruiter Messages (No Applications)
description:
He Stopped Applying And Recruiters Started Messaging Him On LinkedIn


John sent over 200 applications and heard nothing back. Then he changed 4 things on his LinkedIn profile and got 19 messages from recruiters in 6 weeks, one of which became an offer at Citadel. This is how to get noticed by recruiters on LinkedIn, built from what I actually see inside LinkedIn Recruiter, the £9,000 a year software recruiters use to find candidates.

If you are applying constantly and hearing nothing, you are probably not being rejected. You are not being found. This video covers how to get a job on LinkedIn without applying, how recruiter search ranks profiles, the 4 LinkedIn profile changes that made John findable, and the 2 settings almost every job seeker gets wrong.


What you'll learn in this video:
- How LinkedIn Recruiter ranks profiles, and why recruiters only ever message the top 15 results
- The 1 job title rule that took John from invisible to 19 inbound recruiter messages in 6 weeks
- How to get noticed by recruiters using the 4 hard skills they actually type into search
- Why knockout questions reject your applications, not the ATS
- The Open to Work setting to use, and the green banner that gets you filtered out


VIDEO CHAPTERS:
0:00 19 recruiter messages and an offer at Citadel
0:21 You are not being rejected, you are not being found
0:52 What LinkedIn Recruiter costs and what it does
1:16 The tickbox column that decides your ranking
2:11 Why recruiters can only message 15 people
2:48 Knockout questions, not the ATS
3:11 Change 1: one job title, everywhere
5:24 Change 2: the 4 hard skills that get you found
7:08 Put your CV in the Featured section
7:49 Change 3: your how and your why
8:46 The headlines that kill your profile
10:11 Change 4: Open to Work and the 7 day filter
11:05 John's inbox, 19 messages in 6 weeks
11:22 Do this today


Fixed your profile and still not getting found? Find out what is actually costing you the interviews:

CONNECT WITH ME
LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/olivercordingley
Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/olivercordingley


WATCH NEXT:
Why Nobody Replies to Your LinkedIn DMs | The Cold Message Formula That Gets Replies

I dropped out of university at 19 to build recruitment software and ATS systems used by hiring teams. title: Stop Applying To More Jobs | Why You Can't Get A Job Right Now
description:
Stop Applying To More Jobs | Why You Can't Get A Job Right Now


Why is it so hard to get a job in 2026? The honest answer is that the volume strategy everyone still teaches, just apply to more jobs, is now working against you. When you apply to 11 to 20 roles you get an interview from around 9% of them; push past 100 applications and that rate drops below 3%. This video breaks down the 3 things that actually get you hired now: targeting one role, getting warm before you apply, and building one strong core CV.

It's built on a real story. Tim sent over 200 applications and got 2 interviews and zero offers. Six weeks after he stopped applying and switched to a targeted networking system, he had an offer from J.P. Morgan. Here's exactly what changed, and how to do the same.


What you'll learn in this video:
- Why applying to more jobs now lowers your interview rate (9% vs under 3%)
- How to target one role and one industry instead of spraying the whole market
- What a "warm" application really means, and why 65% of jobs are filled through networks
- How Tim landed J.P. Morgan with zero applications through the normal route
- Why tailoring a new CV for every job backfires, and the one core CV approach that works

title: Ghost Jobs: The Real Reason You’re Not Getting Interviews
description:
1 In 3 Jobs You Apply To Are Ghost Jobs


You applied to 30 jobs this month and 9 of them never existed. They were ghost listings: roles already filled, pipeline posts, compliance theatre, or harvests built to collect CVs. Around 30% of UK job postings right now aren't attached to a real, immediate hire. This video shows you the 5 signs a job is a ghost, the 3 channels where the real jobs actually live, and the 48-hour timing rule that decides whether your application even gets read.


What you'll learn in this video:
- What a ghost job actually is, and the 4 types companies post
- The 5 signs a listing is a ghost, so you can spot one in 30 seconds
- Why 30 of every 100 board applications were never going to get a reply
- The 3 channels where real jobs live, and the 30/30/40 time split that works
- The 48-hour rule that decides whether your application even gets read


VIDEO CHAPTERS:
0:00 9 of your 30 applications never existed
1:04 What a ghost job actually is (4 types)
2:35 Sign 1: posted for 30+ days
2:55 Sign 2: generic description
3:14 Sign 3: no named hiring manager
3:34 Sign 4: repeated reposts
3:51 Sign 5: lazy default application form
4:16 Where the real jobs actually live
5:54 The 30/30/40 allocation that works
6:15 The 48-hour rule
7:04 Audit your last 30 applications


Stop pouring applications into listings that were never real, and start spending that time where the offers actually come from. Here's how I can help:

WORK WITH ME:
The Offer Accelerator is my full system for landing offers faster. Personal brand, CV, LinkedIn, networking, applications, interviews, the lot.
https://community.offeraccelerator.co.uk/join?invitation_token=31dd2c6ff3c2d29110be25aace66bb325cab07f2-68a0b5d6-d377-438f-bb72-6e0ede239116&utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=description&utm_campaign=1-in-3-jobs-dont-exist


CONNECT WITH ME
LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/olivercordingley
Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/olivercordingley


WATCH NEXT:
Stop Applying Online | How to Land a Job in the Hidden Job Market


ABOUT ME:
I dropped out of university at 19 to build recruitment software and ATS systems used by hiring teams. For years I spoke to hundreds of hiring managers and recruiters every day, learning exactly how candidates get filtered, shortlisted, and hired from the inside. I started coaching friends through their job search using what I'd seen, then raised investment, built a software company, and hired my own team. I've seen hiring from every angle.

Today I help job seekers land offers faster using a proven 3-step system. I've coached hundreds of candidates into roles at firms like JP Morgan, Goldman Sachs, Deloitte, EY, and PwC and many more.

Are you applying to ghost jobs? Learn how to spot fake job postings and save hours on your job search with these practical identification methods.

Ghost jobs are listings that remain active on boards despite companies not actively hiring for the role. With research suggesting nearly 30% of postings fall into this category, understanding the signs of these inactive listings is essential for anyone currently looking for work. This guide breaks down five key indicators to help you avoid wasting time on applications that will never lead to an interview.

We examine common red flags, such as roles posted for over 30 days or positions that appear to be reposted repeatedly. By learning to identify ghost jobs early, you can refine your job search tips and focus your energy on active opportunities. Use these insights to improve your career strategy and filter out listings that are unlikely to result in a hire.
